label: Ceph RBD block-storage connector
summary: Prepare block-image-specific inventory and reviewed attachment/snapshot integration for explicitly owned Ceph RBD resources.
core_boundary: An RBD image is not a CephFS share or RGW/S3 object. Core controls block-device mappings, guest ownership, fencing and recovery; no host device or cluster-admin interface reaches the plugin. This is a design-only connector proposal. Essential hosting, current actor and tenant authorization, native service drivers and recovery remain in the free Core. No production interface, publisher trust, installation or effectful capability is established by this metadata.
acceptance: Qualify a selected image/pool/namespace/client and Core-provider profile with storage capabilities, guest ownership and explicitly supported image features.
Validate active consumers, cooperative versus exclusive access and fencing before attachment or recovery; an exclusive-lock feature is not assumed to make arbitrary multi-writer filesystem use safe.

Exercise stale clients, interrupted snapshots and ambiguous detach; never break locks, blocklist clients, discard images or purge retained snapshots without separately admitted authority and recovery evidence.

Declare observation-only, import or externally managed ownership before any integration request. Refuse competing writers for Core-owned resources; ownership handoff requires an authorized inventory, admission review and recovery plan.

Before implementation, qualify an explicitly selected provider/interface revision, supported compatibility matrix, immutable package provenance, dependency inventory and licensing model; no release is admitted by this proposal.

Enforce current Core actor, tenant and capability checks at each admitted request; keep credentials in scoped secret references, redact diagnostics and reject arbitrary destinations, shell commands or host/container sockets.

Demonstrate that disablement, removal, provider outage and commercial entitlement loss preserve essential Core access, hosted workloads, local audit and recovery; retain owned data unless a separately authorized purge is requested.
